title: The Intact Web
mechanism: Absence of disturbance: an unbroken spider web across a cellar door proves nobody used it, so the neighbour who claims to have seen an intruder enter there invented him.

seg.hook: A burglar came through the cellar door. Or so one man says. A spider disagrees.
seg.case: Marsh Cottage, three in the morning. A silver clock vanishes. The cellar door has been locked all week. Across its frame, from side to side, hangs a spider's web.
seg.s1: Dora, the cleaner: "I have the front door key. I was asleep at home."
seg.s2: Emil, the gardener: "My boots are muddy from the garden. That's all."
seg.s3: Fritz, the neighbor: "I saw it from my window. A man opened the cellar door and slipped inside."
seg.challenge: Who invented the burglar? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Fritz. Anyone opening that door would have torn the web. It was perfectly whole. Nobody used that door. Dora's key and Emil's boots were false leads. Only the thief needed an invented burglar.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Sydney Breakfast
mechanism: Time-zone arithmetic: at 11 PM in London it is 6 PM in New York, 8 AM in Tokyo and 10 AM in Sydney, so a Sydney brother going to bed contradicts the claimed call.
q: Who was never on that call?

seg.hook: Three alibis in three time zones. One of them cannot be true.
seg.case: A flat in London is burgled at exactly eleven at night. Three friends say they were on a video call at that very minute. New York is five hours behind London. Tokyo is nine ahead. Sydney is eleven ahead.
seg.s1: Mei called her mother in New York. She was cooking dinner.
seg.s2: Noel called his friend in Tokyo. He was making his morning coffee.
seg.s3: Pru called her brother in Sydney. He was just going to bed.
seg.challenge: Who was never on that call? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Pru. Eleven at night in London is ten in the morning in Sydney. Her brother was not going to bed. Dinner in New York at six, and coffee in Tokyo at eight, both fit perfectly.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Daffodil Photo
mechanism: Seasonal botany: daffodils bloom in March-April, so a selfie 'dated 3 November' in London showing daffodils in full bloom is months old with an edited date stamp.
q: Whose photo is not from that day?

seg.hook: Three selfies, all dated the same day. One of them is from another season.
seg.case: A jewelry shop in London is robbed on the third of November. Each suspect shows a park selfie, stamped that very day.
seg.s1: Gus: "Look at my photo. Red leaves are all over the ground."
seg.s2: Ida: "Look at mine. Bare trees, and bright holly berries."
seg.s3: Jon: "Look at mine. A field of yellow daffodils in full bloom."
seg.challenge: Whose photo is not from that day? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Jon. Daffodils bloom in spring, in March or April, never in November. His photo was months old, and he edited the date stamp. Red leaves and holly berries belong to autumn.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Jerry Can
mechanism: Capacity arithmetic: a 35-litre tank cannot take a 60-litre purchase, so the surplus went into a can for the arson.
q: Who bought fuel for the fire?

seg.hook: Everybody fills a tank. Only one person filled something else.
seg.case: A barn burns down at midnight. The fire marshal smells gasoline, a lot of it. Three neighbors show a fuel receipt from that evening, all from the same station.
seg.s1: Kay drives a family car with a forty-five liter tank. Her receipt: forty liters.
seg.s2: Len rides a motorbike with a fifteen liter tank. His receipt: fourteen liters.
seg.s3: Mo drives a small hatchback with a thirty-five liter tank. His receipt: sixty liters.
seg.challenge: Who bought fuel for the fire? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Mo. A thirty-five liter tank cannot hold sixty liters. Twenty-five liters went into a can. Kay and Len bought less than their tanks hold.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Wrong Sunrise
mechanism: Cardinal geography: the sun rises in the east, so a sunrise rising out of the sea cannot be filmed on a west-facing coast like Santa Monica.
board: THE SUN RISES IN THE EAST

seg.hook: One sunrise video cannot be real. The sun rose on the wrong side.
seg.case: A mansion is robbed at dawn. Three suspects say they were on faraway beaches, filming the sun rise out of the sea. Remember: the sun always rises in the east.
seg.s1: Nat: "I was at Santa Monica, on the west coast of California."
seg.s2: Olive: "I was at Miami Beach, on the east coast of Florida."
seg.s3: Pat: "I was at Bondi Beach, on the east coast of Australia."
seg.challenge: Whose sunrise cannot be real? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Nat. On California's west coast, the sea lies to the west. The sun rises behind the land, never out of the water. Olive and Pat faced east, so their sunrises over the sea were possible.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Pearl Test
mechanism: Material test: real pearls feel gritty when rubbed on the teeth, glass or plastic imitations feel smooth; weight and shine can be faked.

seg.hook: Two necklaces are glass. One is the stolen pearls. The test uses your teeth.
seg.case: The Duchess's pearls vanish from the museum. Three curators each keep a necklace at home. Two are glass copies. One is the real thing.
seg.s1: Qin's necklace is the heaviest. Rubbed on a tooth, it feels perfectly smooth.
seg.s2: Ruth's necklace is the shiniest. Rubbed on a tooth, it feels perfectly smooth.
seg.s3: Sam's necklace is dull and plain. Rubbed on a tooth, it feels gritty, like fine sand.
seg.challenge: Whose pearls are real? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Sam. Real pearls feel gritty against the teeth. Glass and plastic are smooth. Weight and shine can be faked, and Qin and Ruth's glass proved it.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Missing Thirteenth
mechanism: Building convention: a hotel with no thirteenth floor makes 'room 1307' nonexistent, exposing an invented alibi.

seg.hook: An alibi in a room that does not exist. Count the floors.
seg.case: A guest is robbed at the Alder Hotel, between midnight and one. The elevator buttons read twelve, fourteen, fifteen. Like many hotels, the Alder has no thirteenth floor.
seg.s1: Tess: "I was in room twelve oh seven, watching television."
seg.s2: Uli: "I was in room thirteen oh seven, on the phone."
seg.s3: Vince: "I was in room fourteen oh seven, asleep. Nobody can confirm it."
seg.challenge: Who invented an alibi? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Uli. The Alder skips the thirteenth floor, so room thirteen oh seven does not exist. Vince's missing witness was a false lead. Uli made up a room to hide where he really was.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Egg That Floated
mechanism: Egg freshness: a fresh egg sinks and lies flat, an old egg takes in air and floats, so eggs claimed as gathered at dawn but floating are weeks old.

seg.hook: Three baskets of eggs. One egg floats. That is the liar.
seg.case: The farmer is found dead in the barn at dawn. Three workers say they spent that dawn in the henhouse, gathering eggs. The inspector drops one egg from each basket into a bowl of water.
seg.s1: Abel: "I gathered mine at sunrise." His egg sinks, and lies flat.
seg.s2: Cass: "I gathered mine at first light." Her egg sinks, and lies flat.
seg.s3: Dev: "I filled my basket before anyone was up." His egg floats to the top.
seg.challenge: Who lied about the henhouse? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Dev. A fresh egg is heavy and sinks. As an egg ages, air seeps through the shell, and it floats. Dev's eggs were weeks old. He never gathered them that dawn.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Short Ladder
mechanism: Ladder geometry: a safely leaned 4 m ladder reaches under 4 m, so a 5 m sill cannot be reached; the window was opened from inside by the keyholder.

seg.hook: A ladder against a wall. Too short to matter. Do the math.
seg.case: A necklace vanishes from a second-floor bedroom. The window sill is five meters above the ground. Below it, a four meter ladder leans against the wall. The window is open. The front door shows no force.
seg.s1: Fay, the neighbor: "That's my ladder. Somebody took it from my shed."
seg.s2: Hugo, the gardener: "I trim the hedge. I have no keys to the house."
seg.s3: Jude, the housekeeper: "I have keys to the house. I was home all night."
seg.challenge: Who opened that window? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Jude. A four meter ladder, leaned safely against a wall, reaches less than four meters. The sill is five. Nobody climbed it. The window was opened from inside, with a key. Fay's ladder was a false lead.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Falling Horn
mechanism: Doppler effect: a sound source moving away drops in pitch, so a witness describing a rising horn as the car left was never on the porch.
q: Who was never on that porch?

seg.hook: A horn rising in pitch as the car drove away. That is impossible.
seg.case: Midnight. A getaway car races away from the bank, horn blaring. Three neighbors say they stood on their porches and watched it drive away from them.
seg.s1: Kira: "The horn sounded lower and lower as it left."
seg.s2: Lou: "The horn rose higher and higher as it sped away."
seg.s3: Mace: "Loud at first, then lower, then quiet, as it left."
seg.challenge: Who was never on that porch? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Lou. When a sound moves away from you, its pitch drops. It only rises while it comes toward you. That is the Doppler effect. Lou described something he never heard.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Wrong Buttons
mechanism: Clothing convention: men's coats have the buttons on the wearer's right, women's on the left, so a 'woman' in a right-buttoned coat is a man in a wig.
board: CAMERA: A WIG, A LONG COAT

seg.hook: The camera saw a woman. Her coat buttons say otherwise.
seg.case: A painting is stolen from a gallery. The camera catches a figure in a wig and a long coat, slipping out the back. The buttons run down the wearer's right side.
seg.s1: Nell, the receptionist: "I own a red coat. I was at the front desk."
seg.s2: Opal, the guide: "I'm the tallest woman here. I was in the cloakroom."
seg.s3: Rhys, the guard: "I was on my rounds in the east wing, alone."
seg.challenge: Who wore that coat? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Rhys. Women's coats button on the wearer's left. Men's coats, on the right. The thief wore a woman's wig, but a man's coat. Nell's red coat and Opal's height were false leads.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.

title: The Southern Cross
mechanism: Celestial geography: the Southern Cross is not visible from high northern latitudes, so a stargazing photo of it from Alberta, Canada is fake or from elsewhere.

seg.hook: A photo of the night sky, with the stars in the wrong half of the world.
seg.case: A jewel heist at midnight. Three suspects each send a photo of the night sky from far away. The Big Dipper hangs in the northern sky. The Southern Cross shines only in the south.
seg.s1: Sid: "I camped in Scotland. Here's the Big Dipper."
seg.s2: Tam: "I camped in Alberta, Canada. Here's the Southern Cross."
seg.s3: Una: "I camped in the Australian outback. Here's the Southern Cross."
seg.challenge: Whose night sky is fake? You have five seconds. Five. Four. Three. Two. One.
seg.reveal: It was Tam. The Southern Cross never rises over Canada. You must go south, near the equator or beyond, to see it. Una's outback sky was real, and Sid's Big Dipper fits Scotland.
seg.outro: Did you solve it? Comment your answer. This is ClueLab.
